introduction.text: The Gazometro di Roma is a former gasometer located in Rome’s Ostiense district. Built in the 1930s, it was the largest gasometer in Italy and became a symbol of the area’s industrial heritage. In the 21st century it has been transformed into the Luxometro, a contemporary art installation that illuminates the site with LED lights, turning the industrial landmark into a cultural icon.

history.description: Design of the Gazometro was conceived in 1909 by Mayor Ernesto Nathan.
Three smaller gasometers were built by Samuel Cuttler & Sons between 1910 and 1912.
Construction of the main gasometer and its supporting metal framework was carried out by Ansaldo and Klonne Dortmund between 1935 and 1937.
Since 1967 the Gazometro area has been owned by Eni, following its acquisition of Italgas through Snam.
In 2006 the municipality of Rome and Eni launched the Luxometro project, converting the site into a contemporary art installation.
In 2020 Eni opened the Joule business school on the site, an accelerator for sustainable entrepreneurship.
Since 2021 the area hosts ZERO, a cleantech startup accelerator.
The Gazometro hosted Maker Faire Rome in 2021 and 2022.
In 2022 the Eni 2050 Lab was inaugurated in building 30.
On 17 May 2023 the ROAD project was inaugurated, aiming to promote energy innovation.

design.description: The main gasometer had a height of 89.10 m, a diameter of 63 m, and a volume of 200,000 m³, supported by 1,551 steel poles spanning 36 km.
The structure consists of a steel framework that once encircled the gas cylinder, now standing after the cylinder was removed.
The Luxometro installation uses over one million LED lamps arranged along more than ten kilometres of fibre optic cable.

art.description: Luxometro is a contemporary art piece that transforms the Gazometro into a luminous landmark, turning industrial heritage into a visual spectacle.
The LED lighting turns the former gasometer into an icon of cultural and artistic significance in Rome.
